extracted.intended_audience: State and Federal Health Insurance Exchanges, CMS/HHS implementers, issuers, agents/brokers, navigators/assisters, and other stakeholders submitting comments on Exchange eligibility and verification rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed amendments to Exchange regulations implementing APTC/PTC, verification, and related program-integrity provisions to align with recent WFTC legislation and prior Marketplace Integrity and Affordability rules (definitions, SAVE verification, FTR policy, pre-enrollment and income verification, and BHP payment updates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'eligible noncitizen' (§155.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to add a new definition of “eligible noncitizen” at §155.20, providing that the term “eligible noncitizen” would have the same meaning as the term “eligible alien,” as defined in 26 U.S.C. 36B(e)(2)(B) (as amended by section 71301 of the WFTC legislation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns Exchange regulations with Treasury/Code definition created by WFTC section 71301; affects who may receive APTC; effective for plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2027. Also cross-referenced for BHP payment methodology changes (42 CFR 600.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Family definition reference in §155.305(f)(1)(ii)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §155.305(f)(1)(ii) to state a tax filer is eligible for APTC if the Exchange determines that one or more applicants who is a member of the tax filer's family, as defined at 26 CFR 1.36B-1(d), meets QHP enrollment eligibility requirements and is not eligible for MEC during the coverage month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change better aligns Exchange rules with existing Treasury regulations regarding PTC eligibility and provides clearer description of individuals on whose behalf a tax filer may be allowed APTC, given elimination of personal exemptions on federal returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require APTC eligibility for U.S. citizens, nationals, or eligible noncitizens (§155.305(f)(1)(ii)(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to add §155.305(f)(1)(ii)(C) to provide that an Exchange must grant eligibility for APTC to individuals who are U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, or eligible noncitizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This amendment aligns with new eligibility requirements in section 71301 of the WFTC legislation and works with verification requirements described below to confirm immigration status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of eligible noncitizen immigration status via SAVE (§155.320(c)(3)(ix))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to add verification regulations at §155.320(c)(3)(ix) requiring Exchanges to attempt to verify eligible noncitizen immigration status using Department of Homeland Security's SAVE program and to proceed with the inconsistency process in §155.315(f)(1)–(4) when the Exchange cannot verify using SAVE data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes Exchange verification requirements for applicants attesting to eligible noncitizen status; ties into proposed definition at §155.20 and aligns Exchange verification with Treasury/Code changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove duplicative language and add headings in §155.320(c)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove the first occurrence of §155.320(c)(3)(viii) and add headings to §155.320(c)(3)(vii) and (viii) to eliminate redundancy (both provisions intended to define 'family size').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: duplication appeared to be an oversight from previous rulemaking; the regulatory definition in 26 CFR 1.36B-1 is deemed more appropriate for use in Exchange regulations; change is largely technical/clerical to improve clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add 'eligible noncitizen' definition at 42 CFR 600.5 (BHP payment alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to add a definition of 'eligible noncitizen' at 42 CFR 600.5, cross-referencing the definition at 45 CFR 155.20, to align BHP program regulations with the statutory change for Federal funding to States operating BHPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This update affects Federal payments to States (payment methodology) for BHP enrollees who are lawfully present noncitizens but not 'eligible aliens' under the Code; does not change underlying BHP eligibility; effective for plan years starting on or after January 1, 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove §155.305(f)(2) — disallow PTC/APTC for certain lawfully present noncitizens (income <100% FPL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §155.305(f)(2), which previously required Exchanges to determine a tax filer eligible for APTC where household income <100% FPL and a lawfully present noncitizen was ineligible for Medicaid due to immigration status, because 26 U.S.C. 36B(c)(1)(B) was repealed by section 71302 of the WFTC legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns Exchange APTC eligibility rules with the Code; effective for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025 (WFTC section 71302 applicable Jan 1, 2026). Also leads to removal of related SEP trigger language and affects Federal BHP payments for the impacted population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conforming amendments to verification and SEP regs
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose conforming amendments to §155.320(c)(3)(iii)(A) and §155.420(d)(13) to remove references to §155.305(f)(2) and the population described in that provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures internal consistency across verification and special enrollment period rules following removal of §155.305(f)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure To File and Reconcile (FTR) policy — 1-tax year FTR for PY 2028 (with option to early adopt in PY 2027)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to amend §155.305(f)(4) so that in PY 2028 and beyond Exchanges must not determine a tax filer or their enrollee eligible for APTC if HHS notifies the Exchange that APTC were paid for a year and the tax filer (or spouse) did not file a Federal income tax return and reconcile APTC for that year (the '1-tax year FTR' process). Exchanges may elect to early adopt the 1-tax year FTR policy in PY 2027 if capable, or continue a 2-tax year FTR process until PY 2028.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal platform Exchanges would adopt 1-tax year FTR in PY 2027; proposal reorganizes paragraph (f)(4) into Definitions, APTC eligibility, and Notices; rationale centers on preventing accumulation of large tax liabilities and improving program integrity in light of WFTC changes removing certain recapture limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible 1- or 2-tax year FTR operation for PY 2027 and required 1-tax year for PY 2028
rubrics_metrics.description: For PY 2027, an Exchange may choose either the 1-tax year or 2-tax year FTR process; if an Exchange does not adopt 1-tax year for PY 2027, it must operate the 2-tax year process for that year. For PY 2028 and beyond, Exchanges must operate a 1-tax year FTR policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes State Exchanges' varying resources and operational constraints; Federal Exchange expected to early adopt 1-tax year in 2027. Notices to consumers must reflect which policy an Exchange is implementing for PY 2027 and that 1-tax year will be implemented for PY 2028.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTR notice and warning requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Require Exchanges to issue FTR warning notices to enrollees identified as not filing and reconciling for 1-tax year and for 2 consecutive tax years (as previously required in Payment Notices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices were used to mitigate consumer harm and inform accountable taxpayers; prior Payment Notices required warning notices for 1- and 2-tax year FTR statuses to reduce risk of unanticipated tax liabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage month definition tied to implementation of 1-tax year FTR (WFTC §71303)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under WFTC section 71303, for taxable years after December 31, 2027, a month is not a 'coverage month' (and no PTC is payable) for an individual enrolled in a QHP through an Exchange for any month for which the Exchange does not meet the requirements of §155.305(f)(4)(iii) (the 1-tax year FTR policy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory change effectively compels Exchanges to implement the 1-tax year FTR policy by PY 2028 if consumers are to receive APTC for months of coverage; rationale used to argue for earlier implementation to protect consumers from large tax liabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-enrollment verification process requirement (section 71303(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 71303(b) amends the Code to require that any plan enrolled in through an Exchange is not considered a QHP (and no PTC allowed) unless, no later than August 1 of the preceding year, Exchanges provide 'a process for pre-enrollment verification' that permits any applicant to verify household income and eligibility for enrollment for the upcoming plan year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS seeks comment on operational considerations, timelines, communications, complexity, costs, burdens, enrollment impacts, and State-specific considerations for meeting the August 1, 2027, deadline to establish pre-enrollment verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum 'applicable enrollment information' and verification flexibilities (WFTC §71303(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 71303(a) specifies a minimum set of 'applicable enrollment information'; clarifies that a past month may be treated as a coverage month if an Exchange later verifies eligibility; specifies verification requirements do not affect QHP enrollment eligibility; permits the Treasury Secretary to waive verification requirements when an individual qualifies for an SEP based on change in family size; and allows Exchanges to use 'any data available to the Exchange and any reliable third-party sources' for collecting information for verification by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS will issue regulations, guidance, technical assistance, and educational materials to implement these provisions and seeks comment on specifics; the provision provides broad leeway for data sources and potential waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income verification when trusted data indicates income <100% FPL (§155.320(c)(3)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: To require submission of documents to verify income when an applicant's attested projected household income is at or above 100% of the FPL and trusted data sources indicate the consumer's household income is below 100% of the FPL (policy finalized in 2025 Marketplace Integrity and Affordability final rule and proposed for continuation/alignment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy aims to detect improper enrollments (including potentially AI-enabled impersonation and false attestation by agents/brokers) before APTC is paid; the rule had been previously vacated/stayed by courts and HHS describes operational reasons for resuming the verification requirement, balanced against burdens and State-specific experiences with improper enrollments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of trusted federal data sources, issuer reports, and documentation to detect improper enrollments
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will continue to uncover improper enrollments through reports from consumers, agents and brokers, and issuers, and intends to use trusted Federal data sources and documentation requirements to detect suspect attestations (e.g., inflated incomes) and improper enrollments before APTC payments are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS cites examples (agents/brokers/web-brokers using AI to impersonate consumers) and operational experience (large volumes of improper enrollments in 2023–2025) to justify program-integrity verifications; recognizes court stays and seeks comment on operational impacts.
